newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives surge in Scottish opinion poll.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives surge in Scottish opinion poll.

text.p: Britain's ruling Conservatives surged four points in a Scottish opinion poll, its biggest monthly rise for four years, although the party is still third-placed in Scotland.
The System Three poll showed Prime Minister John Major's party with 16 percent voter support while Tony Blair's opposition Labour dropped to 50 percent, down two points.

The survey of voting intentions in the Herald newspaper also showed support for the pro-independence Scottish National Party (SNP) also dropping back two points but retaining second place with 22 percent.
Liberal Democrats were steady on 10 percent.
Scottish party chairman Sir Michael Hirst gave a cautious welcome to the highest level of Conservative support for three years while maintaining opinion polls always underestimated the true level.

Others suggested the rise could reflect a change in the way this month's poll was carried out. For the first time, respondents were asked to use a code letter to indicate the party they would vote for instead of giving the party name.
The survey was carried out in 39 of Scotland's 72 parliamentary seats between January 3 and 8.
Conservatives now have 10 seats, Labour 49, Liberal Democrats 9 and SNP four. An election must be held by May.
